classification.habit: Large perennial twining herb with milky juice and long fleshy roots.
classification.habitat: Hedges, thickets and open waste land in the plains and lower hills.
classification.distribution: Throughout India up to about 900 m; also cultivated.

identification.description: Long fleshy roots with central woody core, longitudinally furrowed dark reddish-brown bark and faint odor.
identification.whole_plant: Twining herb with winged, three-angled stems, heart-shaped leaves and large white funnel-shaped flowers.
identification.root: Cylindrical root pieces 1.5–15 cm long and 1–5 cm thick, dull grey to reddish-grey or light brown, deeply furrowed giving a rope-like look; cut surface shows thick whitish bark and light yellow centre; taste slightly acrid and nauseating (API).
identification.stem: Twining stem with three to four longitudinal wings (hence 'Trivrit'), often reddish, with milky latex.
identification.leaf: Alternate, ovate to cordate leaves, 5–15 cm long, entire or slightly lobed, pubescent.
identification.flower: Large white funnel-shaped flowers in few-flowered axillary cymes, with large persistent sepals.
identification.fruit: Globose capsule enclosed by the enlarged, persistent sepals.
identification.seed: Usually four black, smooth or glabrous seeds per capsule.
identification_points: Thick whitish bark with light yellow central wood

dosha.pitta: pacifies through virechana when appropriately used

therapeutics.dose: Mula churna 1–3 g (API); for virechana 3–6 g
therapeutics.anupana: Ushna jala or Triphala kwatha (for Virechana)
therapeutics.precautions: Purgative drug: give only after assessing Koshtha, Agni and Bala; use under supervision for Virechana. Excess use can cause dehydration, weakness and Vata aggravation (Trivrit is Vatala).
therapeutics.contraindications: Pregnancy, children, the elderly and debilitated, Atisara and Grahani, Gudabhramsha, rectal bleeding, recent fever with debility, and dehydration.

shlokas:
श्वेता त्रिवृद्रेचनी स्यात्स्वाद्वी उष्णा समीरजित् ।
रूक्षा पित्तज्वरश्लेष्मपित्तशोथोदरापहा ॥

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: The purgative action is due to resinous glycosides (turpeth resin) concentrated in the root bark (API: resinous glycosides).

modern_information.evidence_summary: Operculina turpethum is a strong purgative herb used in Ayurveda for detoxification and relieving constipation.
recognized_uses: Ingredient of Avipattikara Churna for hyperacidity
modern_information.safety_notes: Strong cathartic in higher doses; may cause cramps, diarrhoea and electrolyte loss. Avoid in pregnancy.

doctor.quick_reference: Trivrit root is the classical Sukhavirechana drug (Tikta-Katu, Ushna) used for Virechana in Pitta and Kapha disorders, Vibandha, Udara and Shotha; 1–3 g churna, more only for supervised Virechana.
